To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) for trees, an estimator for the infection source associated with the most probable infection path is a Jordan center; (b) for general networks, an estimator for a Jordan center is a good source estimator; (c) for general networks and limited observations, an estimator that is based on a Jordan center and a distance to a set of observed infected neighbors performs well.
(i) the Jordan center is the optimal estimator for the infection source in a tree network, and (ii) the approximate estimators perform well for general networks.

(1) for a Susceptin-Infected model on a tree, the Jordan center is the most likely infection source node; (2) for a general network, the Jordan center and a node with maximum closeness centrality are the two most likely infection source nodes; and (3) for a Suspectible-Infected-Recovered model, the Jordan center of the recovered subgraph is the most likely source node.
